pattern.top_pattern: OH and UNATTRIBUTED show rare catastrophic IP Med/Surg cases
pattern.what_is_impacting: IP Med/Surg high-cost outlier admissions in OH and UNATTRIBUTED
key_driver_codes: Intracranial Hemorrhage or Cerebral Infarction with MCC
Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with MCC
pattern.pattern_details: This segment is being driven by rare catastrophic inpatient Med/Surg cases, not by broad utilization expansion. The increase is concentrated in only three cases, led by a transplant-sized claim, with additional stroke and severe sepsis admissions. The right response is case-level clinical and payment validation rather than broad benefit or network changes.
pattern.why_it_matters: Catastrophic outliers can materially change trend results even when they are not repeatable patterns.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Open case-level clinical and payment validation for the transplant, stroke, and sepsis admissions to confirm severity, reimbursement accuracy, and any applicable outlier protections.
pattern.validation_reason: The spend is concentrated in a few very high-cost admissions and part of the segment is unattributed, so direct action requires claim-level confirmation.
evidence_summary: A single severe sepsis admission added $30K.
